text: I took ~50 frames of NGC 7789 last night on the 0.6m, r band, 120s each, and before I stack them I have to throw out the bad ones. right now I blink through them in ds9 one at a time and it takes me an hour. I want to see the whole night at once as small images in a grid, with the FWHM, sky background and number of stars detected under each one, and a big version of the one I'm on. then go through with the keyboard, k = keep, r = reject, arrow keys to move. for now fake the frames: random star field (same field every frame, small dither), noise, and put in some bad ones like a real night: a satellite trail or two, a cloud passing over a few frames, trailed stars from the mount slipping, and the hot column we get when the cooler cant keep up
when I reject a frame I want to record why: trail, cloud, blur or other. maybe press r and then 1-4? and show how many we lost to each, the observatory asks for that in the night report

can I sort by fwhm? the seeing went bad for a while around 4 UT and I want the worst ones together. also put up top how many frames I've kept and the total exposure of those, I need at least 45 min in the stack for the faint end of the main sequence

the big view is way too dark, I can only see the bright stars and cant judge the faint ones at all. use an asinh stretch and keep linear as an option. also up/down arrows should go to the row above/below, right now they do nothing

last bit is export. a txt with the kept filenames one per line so I can feed it straight to the stacking script, and a csv of every frame with the numbers and keep/reject + reason so I have a record of the night
